title: Admission images and records classify COVID outcomes across six Italian hospitals
summary: A December 2020 preprint studied admission chest X-rays and records from 820 hospitalized patients. A combined image-feature and clinical classifier reported mean accuracy 0.743 in leave-one-center-out evaluation for a composite severe outcome. This retrospective first-wave study does not establish prospective benefit or superiority over clinical records alone.
ai_technology: Convolutional image features with classical supervised classifiers
organization: University Campus Bio-Medico of Rome; Fondazione Bruno Kessler

source_review.scope: Original v1 archive metadata and PDF clinical-data/model-validation Methods and Tables4/5; exact results compared with later journal full text. Version-header and submission dates remain distinguished.

evidence.tested: The six-hospital cohort had 820 admission examinations, with outcomes classified as mild versus non-invasive ventilation, intensive care or death. Training-fold normalization, feature selection and parameter fitting were described. In original v1 Table 5, GoogleNet image features plus clinical data and logistic regression achieved mean accuracy .743±.061, sensitivity .769±.189 and specificity .685±.155 across held-out centers; clinical-data SVM accuracy was .734±.044. The later August 2021 journal tables retain these values.
evidence.unknown: Many configurations were compared, and displayed best performances do not constitute an untouched locked-model evaluation. Center-held-out evaluation reuses one first-wave study rather than independent replication. Severe outcome combines several care decisions and mortality; the results do not establish time-to-event prognosis, treatment effect, capacity improvement or clinically significant added value over records alone. The v1 archive says submitted December 11, 2020, while its PDF carries a December 14 version header; this entry uses the dated PDF version and does not assert a first-public-day priority. Journal publication was August 28, 2021.
evidence.ai_role: Neural features extracted from admission radiographs were combined with clinical variables by supervised classifiers to estimate the recorded composite outcome.
